title: A tiny router
description:
Turn requests into responses with a routing table, as a small web server does.

```
GET /           -> 200 "Welcome"
GET /hello/ada  -> 200 "Hello, ada"
POST /hello/ada -> 405 Method Not Allowed
GET /missing    -> 404 Not Found
```
hints: Split both path and pattern at `/`; they match when they have the same number of parts and each part is equal or a `:name` (lesson 3.04).
Remember "matched the path but not the method" in a flag to choose between 404 and 405.
requirements: Routes are (method, pattern, handler); a pattern part starting with `:` captures a value.
A path that matches with another method gives 405, no match 404.
The handler returns a `Response { int status; std::string body; }`; build the full response text with `Content-Length`.
stretch: Serve files from a folder for `GET /static/...`, refusing paths with `..`.
